ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, four cubes are stacked in a stepped shape from top to bottom, with side lengths labeled in order as 1, 2, 3, 4. Their left-front vertical edges are aligned. Point X is marked at the left-front upper corner of the topmost cube with side length 1; point Y is marked near the right-side rear lower corner of the bottommost cube with side length 4, that is, it can be understood according to the diagram as the far-end bottom corner of cube No. 4. Reasoning: Establish a three-dimensional coordinate system according to the diagram. Let the bottom cube with side length 4 occupy 0≤x≤4, 0≤y≤4, 0≤z≤4. Because the total height of the four cubes is 4+3+2+1=10, X=(0,0,10), while Y=(4,4,0). Line segment XY can be parameterized as (x,y,z)=(4t,4t,10-10t), where 0≤t≤1. The cube with side length 3 is above cube No. 4 and occupies 0≤x≤3, 0≤y≤3, 4≤z≤7. When entering this cube on the line segment, it must satisfy 4≤10-10t≤7, giving 3/10≤t≤6/10. At this time x=4t and y=4t are both not greater than 3, so the horizontal condition is automatically satisfied. Therefore, the parameter length ratio of line segment XY located inside cube No. 3 is 6/10-3/10=3/10. The length of the entire XY is sqrt(4^2+4^2+10^2)=sqrt(132)=2sqrt(33). The required length is (3/10)·2sqrt(33)=3sqrt(33)/5.

From the text, use edge lengths 1, 2, 3, 4, so the total height from bottom to X is 4+3+2+1=10. Let the bottom 4-cube occupy [0,4] in both horizontal directions and z from 0 to 4. Then X=(0,0,10) and Y=(4,4,0). The line segment is (x,y,z)=(4t,4t,10-10t). The cube of edge length 3 occupies 0≤x≤3, 0≤y≤3, and 4≤z≤7. Intersecting with the line gives 4≤10-10t≤7, so 3/10≤t≤6/10; the horizontal bounds are automatically satisfied. Thus the portion inside the 3-cube is 3/10 of the full segment XY. Since |XY|=sqrt(4^2+4^2+10^2)=2sqrt(33), the required length is (3/10)(2sqrt(33))=3sqrt(33)/5.
